subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a core Gateway control-plane and per-agent runtime split, and what first supported milestone should define the protocol, lifecycle, and trust boundary?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but the next step chooses public protocol, config, security, session-state, deployment, and migration boundaries that automation cannot safely decide.

options.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone for local-split protocol, trust, per-agent lifecycle, and session ownership before container or Kubernetes runners.

options.title: Narrow To Execution Placement
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82017 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84758 as the current scope and defer the broader Gateway/runtime split.

options.title: Defer Core Architecture Change
options.body: Continue supporting multi-gateway and operator workarounds without committing to a first-class distributed runtime boundary now.

recommendation.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone for local-split protocol, trust, per-agent lifecycle, and session ownership before container or Kubernetes runners.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal for the agents command/runtime architecture and authored the related worker-runtime experiment that was closed pending a clearer protocol and ownership model.
